title: PACING GUIDE - GRADE 1 ACADEMIC YEAR 2026-2027
note: parsed verbatim from the pacing-guide workbook (merged cells forward-filled: Week/Date, and a section's text merged up from the rows below it)

items.contents:
1. Language Focus:
- Greetings: Hello/ Hi, Good morning, Good afternoon, Good evening, Good night, ...
- Classroom rules: Be quiet, sit nicely, raise your hand, speak English, be kind, ...
- Color: red, yellow, blue, green, purple, orange, black, white, brown, ...
2 Skills Focus: Listening - Speaking

1. Language Focus:
- Topic: The alphabet (A-Z)
- Structures: Hello. I'm...What's your name? -> I'm.../ My name's ...
2. Skill Focus: Listening & Speaking
- Learn the names of the other students in class
- Ask and answer questions about their names.
- Name the alphabet.
items.outcomes:
1. Language Use:
- Use common greetings such as "Hello," "Hi," "Good morning," "Good afternoon," and "Goodbye.", ...
- Use polite expressions like "Please," and "Thank you," in appropriate situations.
- Identify basic classroom rules and follow classroom rules during activities.
- Recognize and name the numbers from 10 to 20.
- Match numbers with corresponding quantities of objects.
2. Skills:
- Point and say the numbers from 10 to 20
- Say and respond to common greetings
- Listen and follow the classroom rules during the activities
3. Value: Recognize the importance of showing respect to teachers and friends through polite greetings

1. Language Use:
- Identify and name letters of the alphabet when shown flashcards/ pictures.
- Recognize and name their classmates when asked.
- Use greetings and introduce themselves with full sentences.
2. Skills:
- Say the alphabet A–Z in order with correct pronunciation.
- Ask and answer “What’s your name?” correctly in a pair activity.
- Recognize and respond to greetings like “Hello” and “What’s your name?”
3. Value: Practice real-life English greetings with classmates (Communication)

items.contents:
1. Language Focus:
- Numbers 1 to 10 (focus on listening, saying, and recognizing these numbers)
- Number names: One, Two, Three, Four, Five, Six, Seven, Eight, Nine, Ten
- Greetings and polite responses
2.
Vocabulary: Numbers 1 to 10
Listening: Recognizing spoken numbers
Speaking: Pronouncing numbers clearly
Visual Recognition: Identifying the visual form of numbers 1 to 10
items.outcomes:
1. Language Use:
- Identify and name letters of the alphabet when shown flashcards/ pictures.
- Recognize and name their classmates when asked.
- Understand and recognize common greetings like “Hello,” “Hi,” “Good morning,” and “Goodbye.”
- Respond correctly to greetings and introduction questions.
2. Skills:
- Say the alphabet A–Z in order with correct pronunciation.
- Ask and answer “What’s your name?” correctly in a pair activity.
- Recognize and respond to greetings like “Hello” and “What’s your name?”
3. Value: Practice real-life English greetings with classmates (Communication)
items.activities:
Support: Use alphabet/greeting cards and sentence frames to practice letter names and “What’s your name?” – “My name is …”.
Extension: Say A–Z independently; ask and answer greeting questions; role-play short greeting conversations with classmates.

items.contents:
1. Language Focus:
Vocabulary: Names of colors (Red, Blue, Green, etc.)
Colors: Red, Blue, Green, Yellow, Orange, Purple, Pink, Black, White, Brown
Color Objects: Common items associated with these colors (e.g., apple, sky, grass)
2. Skills focus
Listening: Identifying colors when heard
Speaking: Correctly pronouncing color names
Recognition: Associating colors with objects and visual cues
items.outcomes:
1. Language Use:
- Recognize and say 10 color words (red, blue, green, yellow, orange, purple, pink, black, white, brown) when shown colors or pictures, correctly in at least 8/10 words.
- Match colors with common objects (e.g., red–apple, blue–sky, green–grass) using pictures, correctly in at least 4/5 items.
2. Skills:
- Listen and identify colors by pointing to or choosing the correct color, correctly in at least 8/10 items.
- Pronounce color names when shown color cards or objects, clearly and correctly in at least 8/10 words.
- Identify and match colors with objects when shown pictures or real objects, correctly in at least 4/5 items.
3. Value: Practice real-life English greetings with classmates (Communication)
items.activities:
Support: Match color words with objects/pictures; use color cards and visual prompts to identify and say colors.
Extension: Identify and spell colors independently; describe objects using color + object; ask and answer simple questions about colors.

items.contents:
1. Language Focus:
- Concepts: Big, Small, Numbers 1 to 10, Colors (Red, Blue, Green, etc.)
- Phrases: Combining size, color, and numbers (e.g., “big red 3,” “small blue 5”)
2. Skills focus:
- Vocabulary: Big, Small, Numbers 1 to 10, Colors
- Listening: Identifying size, color, and number when spoken
- Speaking: Correctly using and combining size, color, and numbers in phrases
- Visual Recognition: Associating and describing objects with size, color, and numbers
items.outcomes:
1. Language Use:
- Recognize and say big, small, numbers 1–10, and basic colors when shown pictures or objects, correctly in at least 8/10 items.
- Combine size, color, and numbers in simple phrases (e.g., big red 3, small blue 5) when describing pictures, in at least 3 phrases.
2. Skills:
- Listen and identify the correct size, color, and number by pointing to or choosing pictures, correctly in at least 4/5 items.
- Describe objects using size + color + number (e.g., big red 3) when shown pictures, in at least 3 phrases.
- Match and describe objects with their size, color, and number using picture cues, correctly in at least 4/5 items.
3. Value:
items.activities:
Support: Use picture/number/color cards to identify and match objects; practice “big/small + color + number” with sentence frames.
Extension: Describe objects independently using size, color and number; create and describe their own combinations.

items.contents:
1. Language Focus:
- The differences between living and non-living things
- Vocabulary:
+ look: to use your eyes to find things out.
+ alive: something that is living
+ plant: a living thing that can make its own food
+ animal: a living thing that eats other living things
+ living: living things grow, need food, make waste, use air and reproduce
+ non-living: something that is not alive.
items.outcomes:
1. Language Use:
- Name four or more things that are living.
- Put things into two groups.
- Identify and differentiate between living and non-living things
- Understanding basic characteristics of living things.
items.activities:
Support: Sort picture cards into living/non-living groups; name living things with visual prompts.
Extension: Explain why things are living/non-living; identify basic characteristics and give examples independently.

items.contents:
1. Contents:
- Vocabulary: desk, dog, door, duck
- Sentence pattern: This is a dog.
- Phonic /b/
2. Skills focus: Listening & Speaking
- Students will be able to say names and name familiar objects that start with "d".
items.outcomes:
1. Language Use:
Recognize and say the words desk, dog, door, duck when shown pictures or objects, correctly in at least 3/4 words.
Identify and pronounce the letter D/d and its /d/ sound in target words after teacher modeling, correctly in at least 3/4 attempts.
Use “This is a ___.” to name familiar objects when shown pictures, in at least 3 sentences.
2. Skills:
- Listen and identify words beginning with /d/ by pointing to the correct picture, correctly in at least 3/4 items.
- Name familiar objects beginning with /d/ when shown pictures or real objects, correctly in at least 3 words.
- Say “This is a ___.” to describe familiar objects with picture support, in at least 3 sentences.
3. Value:

items.contents:
1. Language Focus
- Vocabulary:
+ Common nouns for familiar objects, food, and animals (e.g., fish, bear, book, orange,...)
+ Colours (e.g., red, blue, green, yellow)
+ Prepositions of place: under, next to, on, in
- Structures:
+ What is this? / It’s a (book).
+ What colour is it? / It’s (yellow).
+ Put the (bear) under the (table).
2. Skill Focus
- Listening:
+ Understanding and responding to simple instructions (e.g., “Point to the ball.”)
+ Comprehending questions about objects, food, and animals in a picture
- Speaking:
+ Answering basic WH-questions about familiar objects
+ Describing objects using simple adjectives (e.g., colour, size)
+ Using prepositions to describe location
- Comprehension & Interaction:
+ Demonstrating understanding by pointing, placing, or moving objects
+ Participating in guided dialogue and interactive tasks with the teacher
items.outcomes:
1. Language Use
- Recognize and name familiar food (e.g. orange, bread, watermelon, etc.) at a supermarket
- Use simple prepositions (e.g., under, next to, on) to describe the location of objects.
- Respond to basic WH- questions (e.g., “What is this?”, “What colour is it?”) using short, clear phrases or full sentences.
2. Skills
- Listening: listen and respond appropriately to teacher instructions and questions (e.g., pointing, placing objects).
- Speaking: practice clear articulation of familiar words and simple sentences when identifying and describing objects.
- Following Instructions: follow spoken instructions to manipulate objects and demonstrate understanding.
- Interaction and Communication: engage in simple back-and-forth exchanges, helping develop turn-taking and confidence in spoken English.

items.contents:
1. Language Focus:
- Vocabulary: objects (apple, ball, book, cat), colors, family/house words, school-related words.
- Structures:
+ What’s this? – It’s a ball.
+ What color is it? – It’s red.
+ Do you like…? – Yes, I do. / No, I don’t.
+ Do you live in a house or a flat? – I live in a house.
+ Who lives in your house? – My mom/dad…
+ Is your teacher a man or a woman? – He’s a man. / She’s a woman.
2. Skills Focus:
- Listening: Identifying words/questions.
- Speaking: Responding with short, clear answers.
- Reading: Recognizing words/phrases on cards or board.
- Interaction: Asking peers personal and object-based questions.
items.outcomes:
1. Language Use:
- Name basic objects/colors, describe them, express likes/dislikes,
- Answer simple personal questions about home, family, and school.
2. Skills:
- Listen and understand simple classroom questions.
- Respond clearly with short answers.
- Practice peer-to-peer interaction using target structures.
- Gain confidence speaking in pairs and groups.
items.activities:
- Observation
- Oral Q&A Game
- Pair work

items.contents:
1. Language Focus:
- Parts of a plant: stem, root, leave, flower
- Observation of Similarities and Differences: While different plants may look different, they all have the same basic parts.
- Roots, stems, leaves, and flowers in different types of plants (e.g., tomato, bean, strawberry...).
items.outcomes:
1. Language Use
- Recognize and name the basic parts of a plant (root, stem, leaves, flower)
2. Skills
- Draw parts of a plant
- Collect and record onservation

items.contents:
1. Language Focus:
- Vocabulary: bag, book, crayon, eraser, pen, pencil, pencil case, ruler
2. Skill Focus:
- Recognize and understand the meaning of the target vocabulary words.
- Associate the spoken words with the visual images of the objects.
- Practice pronouncing the vocabulary words correctly.
- Recognize Written Words
- Write Basic Words
items.outcomes:
1. Language Use
- Identify and name common school items, such as bag, book, crayon, eraser, pen, pencil, pencil case, and ruler.
- Pronounce the vocabulary words correctly with teacher modeling and repetition.
- Recognize and match written words to corresponding objects or pictures.
- Write basic vocabulary words with support (e.g., copying, tracing, or writing from memory).
2. Skills
- Listening: Understand spoken vocabulary words and associate them with the correct images.
- Speaking: Practice saying vocabulary words clearly and confidently.
- Reading: Recognize written forms of the target vocabulary.
- Writing: Copy or write simple vocabulary words related to school items.
3. Values
- Show interest and motivation in learning English through engaging vocabulary activities.
- Demonstrate focus and responsibility by completing vocabulary practice tasks carefully.
- Build confidence in using new words through active participation and repeated practice.

items.contents:
1. Language Focus:
- Vocabulary:
+ Key school-related words: poster, board, chair, desk
+ Colors: black, green, red, white, yellow
- Structures:
"Can you see a [poster]?"
"I can see a [board]."
2. Skill Focus:
- Vocabulary Development:
+ Identifying and understanding the meaning of key vocabulary related to school items.
+ Associating pictures with their corresponding words.
- Reading Skills:
+ Reading simple sentences about school items.
+ Recognizing and understanding vocabulary in context.
+ Understanding basic information from sentences about school items.
items.outcomes:
1. Language Use
- Recognize and name key school items (poster, board, chair, desk) and colors (black, green, red, white, yellow).
- Understand and use basic phrases related to school items.
- Pronounce the key vocabulary words correctly.
- Trace or write the key vocabulary words correctly.
2. Skills
- Match vocabulary words with their corresponding pictures.
- Read simple sentences about school items with understanding.
- Demonstrate comprehension by answering basic questions about the picture.
3. Values
- Demonstrate curiosity and observation skills when identifying items in the classroom or pictures.
- Practice respect and cooperation by taking turns and listening to others during class discussions or games.

items.contents:
1. Language Focus:
- Vocabulary: common school items (school, bus, pencil, bag)
- Structures:
"What’s this?" / "It’s a [pencil case]."
"Is it a [pencil case]?" / "Yes, it is." / "No, it isn't."
- Values Focus: Emphasizing the importance of taking care of personal belongings, especially school items.
2. Skill Focus:
- Listening Skills:
+ Understanding and following the lyrics of the song.
+ Identifying and repeating the vocabulary for school items.
- Speaking Skills:
+ Singing along with the song, focusing on clear pronunciation of the vocabulary.
+ Practicing the phrases that promote taking care of school things.
items.outcomes:
1. Language Use
- Use the question "What’s this?" and respond with "It’s a [school item]."
- Use the yes/no question form "Is it a [school item]?" and respond appropriately with "Yes, it is." or "No, it isn’t."
- Identify and name common school items such as school, bus, pencil, bag.
- Use language to express ideas about school objects and ownership.
2. Skills
- Listening:
+ Understand and follow the lyrics of a song.
+ Recognize and repeat vocabulary related to school items.
- Speaking: Sing along to practice pronunciation and rhythm.
3. Values
- Develop a sense of responsibility by understanding the importance of taking care of personal and school belongings.
- Show respect for shared classroom materials and others’ belongings.
- Build positive attitudes toward learning through music and participation in class activities.

items.contents:
1. Language Focus:
- Vocabulary Words: light, sunlight, grow, plant, dark, small leaves, big leaves, tall stem, short stem, green leaves, yellow leaves
- Simple Sentences:
“Plants need light to grow.”
“Sunlight helps plants make food.”
“With light, plants have big leaves.”
“Without light, plants may have small leaves.”
“Plants with light have green leaves.”
items.outcomes:
1. Language Use
- Identify and name key vocabulary related to plants and light.
- Use simple sentences to describe how plants use light to grow.
- Identify and use vocabulary related to how light affects plant characteristics.
- Describe the difference in plant characteristics with and without light using simple sentences.

items.contents:
1. Language Focus:
- Letters: a, b, c, d
- Sound: initial sounds /æ/, /b/, /k/, and /d/
- Vocabulary: apple, bag, carrot, desk
2. Skill Focus:
- Developing the ability to hear and identify specific sounds (/æ/, /b/, /k/, and /d/) at the beginning of words.
- Identifying the letters A, B, C, and D visually and associating them with their corresponding sounds.
- Practicing the correct articulation of sounds and words that begin with /æ/ (e.g., apple), /b/ (e.g., bag), /k/ (e.g., carrot), and /d/ (e.g., desk).
- Tracing and independently writing the letters A, B, C, and D with proper formation.
- Recognizing and connecting the written form of letters to pictures and words that begin with the corresponding sounds.
items.outcomes:
1. Language Use
- Identify the sounds /æ/, /b/, /k/, and /d/ at the beginning of words.
- Recognize and orally identify the letters A, B, C, and D.
- Recognize and match words that begin with the sounds /æ/, /b/, /k/, and /d/ to the corresponding letters.
- Pronounce words that begin with the sounds /æ/, /b/, /k/, and /d/ correctly.
2. Skills
- Listening: Distinguish beginning sounds in spoken words.
- Speaking: Practice correct pronunciation of target initial sounds.
- Reading: Identify and associate letters with initial sounds in words.
- Writing: Demonstrate the ability to trace and independently write letters A, B, C, and D.
3. Values
- Show perseverance and effort when practicing handwriting and pronunciation.
- Develop confidence in identifying and producing letter sounds.
- Demonstrate responsibility and independence in completing phonics tasks.

items.contents:
1. Language Focus:
- Vocabulary: common toy names (ball, bat, doll, game, teddy bear, plane, kite, train, etc)
- Grammar:
+ Simple present tense structures (e.g., ""This is a ball,"").
+ Basic questions and answers (e.g., ""Is it a ball?"" - ""Yes it is."").
2. Skill Focus:
- Listening Skills:
+ Listening to identify and recognize toy names.
+ Distinguishing between similar-sounding words.
- Speaking Skills:
+ Pronouncing toy names clearly.
+ Asking and answering simple questions about toys.
- Reading Skills: Recognizing and matching toy names with their corresponding pictures.
- Writing Skills: Marking correct and incorrect responses based on listening and visual cues.
items.outcomes:
1. Language Use
- Use the structure “This is a [toy name]” to describe toys.
- Ask and answer simple questions using “Is it a [toy name]?” – “Yes, it is.” / “No, it isn’t.”
- Recognize and name common toys such as ball, bat, doll, game, teddy bear, plane, kite, train, etc.
- Distinguish between similar-sounding toy words (e.g., ball vs. doll).
2. Skills
- Listening: Identify and understand toy vocabulary when heard; recognize correct and incorrect responses.
- Speaking: Clearly pronounce toy names; ask and answer basic questions using target structures.
- Reading: Match toy names with their corresponding images.
- Writing: Mark correct/incorrect answers based on listening and visual input; copy or trace toy words if applicable.
3. Values
- Demonstrate respect when taking turns during speaking activities and games.
- Build confidence in using English to communicate about familiar, fun topics.
- Develop cooperation and friendliness by working with peers in pair or group tasks related to toys.

items.contents:
1. Language Focus:
- Vocabulary Words: marble, favourite, fun, ball, color, game, small
- Grammar: Understanding sentence structure in the reading text.
2. Skill Focus:
- Listening:
+ Listening to the pronunciation of new vocabulary.
+ Listening to the short text being read aloud.
- Speaking: Repeating vocabulary words and using them in simple sentences.
- Reading:
+ Reading and identifying vocabulary words in a simple text.
+ Understanding the meaning of the text and completing tasks based on it.
- Writing:
+ Practicing spelling of the new words.
+ Completing tasks related to the reading.
items.outcomes:
1. Language Use
Recognize and use key vocabulary related to toys and play in simple spoken and written sentences.
Recognize and apply basic sentence structures from the reading text.
Spell target vocabulary correctly.
2. Skills
Listen and identify target vocabulary and the main idea of a short text.
Pronounce and use target vocabulary in simple oral responses.
Read and locate key information in a short text.
Complete simple writing tasks using target vocabulary and sentence structures.
3. Values
Show enthusiasm when sharing personal interests.
Show confidence when expressing preferences and ideas in English.

items.contents:
1. Language Focus:
- Vocabulary: seed, soil, water, grow, plant, sun, thirsty, drink, plant, flower, tree, leaf, stem, sprout, wilted, dry, healthy.
- Phrases:
"We plant the seed in the soil."
“Plants need water to grow.”
“Seeds grow into plants.”
“Plants are thirsty and drink water.”
"We water the plants to help them grow.”
"The plant is healthy because it gets sunlight."
"This plant is wilted because it is dry.""
"The leaves are green, so the plant is healthy."
items.outcomes:
1. Language Use
- Identify and say the basic words related to plants and water (plant, seed, water, grow).
- Understand and say simple phrases about plants needing water to grow.
- Recognize the process of a seed turning into a plant, emphasizing the role of water.
- Actively participate in a short conversation about how plants need water.
2. Skills
- Observe and describe plants using appropriate vocabulary (healthy, wilted, sprout, etc.).
- Compare plants in different environments and explain how water and sunlight affect their health.
- Gain confidence in sharing observations and applying vocabulary in a real-world context.

items.contents:
1. Language Focus:
- Vocabulary: ball, plane, bat, train, doll, kite, teddy bear
- Grammar Structures:
"Is that a [toy]?" / "Yes, it is." / "No, it isn't."
"It’s a [toy]." / "This is my [toy]."
2. Skill Focus:
- Listening: Listening to and understanding toys mentioned in the video.
- Reading: Reading the lyrics to recognize vocabulary.
- Speaking:
+ Practicing the grammar structures by singing the song.
+ Practicing asking and answering questions using ""Is that a...?"" and other structures.
- Drawing: Drawing and sharing about their favorite toys.
items.outcomes:
1. Language Use
Recognize and say toy vocabulary (ball, plane, bat, train, doll, kite, teddy bear) correctly in at least 6/7 words.
Ask and answer “Is that a …?” – “Yes, it is./No, it isn’t.” with picture support, in at least 3 exchanges.
Use “It’s a …” / “This is my …” to describe toys and possessions in at least 3 sentences.
2. Skills
Listen and identify toy vocabulary and target structures from a short song or video, correctly in at least 4/5 items.
Listen and respond to simple questions about toys with an appropriate answer, correctly in at least 3/4 questions.
Read and recognize toy vocabulary in short texts or song lyrics correctly in at least 6/7 words.
Match toy names or simple sentences with pictures correctly in at least 4/5 items.
Pronounce and repeat toy vocabulary clearly, correctly in at least 6/7 words.
3. Values
Communicate and collaborate with classmates when sharing and talking about toys.

items.contents:
1. Language Focus:
- Phonics:
+ Initial sounds of e, f, g, h (beginning sounds in words).
+ Recognition of uppercase and lowercase letters (E, F, G, H / e, f, g, h).
- Vocabulary Examples:
e: egg, elephant
f: fish, frog
g: goat, girl
h: hat, horse
- Writing: Letter formation of e, f, g, h in both uppercase and lowercase.
2. Skill Focus:
- Listening: Listening to the pronunciation of the initial sounds.
- Speaking: Repeating the sounds and practicing the pronunciation of words starting with e, f, g, h.
- Phonemic Awareness: Identifying the initial sounds in words.
- Writing: Practicing correct formation of both uppercase and lowercase letters.
- Visual Recognition: Differentiating between uppercase and lowercase letters.
items.outcomes:
1. Language Use
Recognize and pronounce the initial sounds /e/, /f/, /g/, /h/ in target words, correctly in at least 4/4 sounds.
Recognize and name vocabulary beginning with E/e, F/f, G/g, H/h (egg, fish, goat, hat) correctly in at least 6/8 words.
Match uppercase and lowercase letters E/e, F/f, G/g, H/h correctly in at least 4/4 pairs.
Use target vocabulary in simple spoken phrases in at least 3 phrases.
2. Skills
Listen and identify the initial sounds /e/, /f/, /g/, /h/ in spoken words correctly in at least 4/5 items.
Match initial sounds to the correct letters E/e, F/f, G/g, H/h, correctly in at least 4/5 items.
Repeat and pronounce target sounds and vocabulary clearly after teacher modeling, correctly in at least 6/8 words.

3. Values
- Perseverance and care in practicing correct letter formation.
- Confidence in speaking and participating in phonics activities.

items.contents:
1. Language Focus:
Classroom Language (Teacher to Student):
"Open/Close your books"
"Raise your hand"
"Stand up/Sit down"
"Come in"
"Please"
"Thank you"
2. Skill Focus:
- Listening: Identify and understand common classroom instructions.
- Reading: Match classroom phrases with corresponding pictures.
- Speaking: Practice responding to classroom instructions.
items.outcomes:
1. Language Use
- Understand and use basic classroom instructions such as “Open your books,” “Sit down,” and “Raise your hand.”
- Recognize polite expressions such as “Please” and “Thank you.”
- Respond appropriately to simple imperative sentences in a classroom context.
2. Skills
- Listening: Identify and follow basic oral classroom instructions.
- Reading: Match simple classroom commands with corresponding images.
- Speaking: Respond orally to teacher instructions using appropriate phrases or actions.
3. Values
- Show respect and cooperation by listening and responding politely to classroom commands.
- Demonstrate classroom behavior such as raising hands and saying “Please” and “Thank you.”
- Develop responsibility by following rules and instructions during class activities.

items.contents:
1. Language Focus:
Identify the role of a gardener.
Understand that gardeners help plants grow by giving them water and sunlight.
2. Skills:
Listen and respond to simple classroom instructions.
Follow simple planting steps.
Plant a seedling independently with teacher guidance.
Present their finished plant using simple English.
